spec_match.rationale: Shows the product-level consequence of the spec contract: the body-consuming loop's catch handler branches on the forwarded reason (custom UserCancel object, TimeoutError from AbortSignal.timeout) versus the pre-153 generic AbortError plus signal.reason workaround.

interactive.rationale: Start/cancel/timeout buttons drive a real streaming download with a live progress bar and byte/chunk readout; every outcome branch renders what catch(err) actually received.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises a download whose catch handler branches on the reason including the pre-153 workaround; the page delivers exactly that plus completion.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers completion without abort, user cancel, real AbortSignal.timeout, endpoint failure, and the timeout-run case where no controller exists for the workaround — surfaced as 'exactly the problem'.

references.rationale: Links MDN AbortSignal.timeout, the fetch spec abort steps, and the sibling probe; the feature index carries the ChromeStatus link.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's timeout-reason-forwards-to-body assertion pins the TimeoutError propagation this page demonstrates; it fails honestly on this pre-153 engine.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP driver run 2026-08-16 (f1-download.png): cancel run hit the generic branch showing catch received AbortError while signal.reason held UserCancel{bytes:264,chunks:3}; timeout run showed the no-controller-in-scope message; a full run completed at 730 bytes/7 chunks; zero console errors, ERR_ABORTED only from the intentional aborts.

telemetry_health.rationale: Distinct asserts per branch (download-completed, download-cancel-reason-forwarded, download-timeout-reason-forwarded, download-generic-fallback, download-setup-error); fallback branches never report as success.

design_system.rationale: Variables only; the secondary cancel button overrides background AND color together per the button-contrast rule; outcome accents are left borders on stone.

accessibility.rationale: role=progressbar with aria-valuenow kept in sync, aria-live polite progress text, role=status outcome panel, native buttons with disabled states and visible focus.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Feature harness passed both classes; controls wrap via flex and the outcome pre wraps long reason serialisations.

openQuestions.title: Exercise the forwarded UserCancel branch on Chrome 153
openQuestions.detail: The cancel and timeout branches currently land in the honest generic-AbortError path on this Chromium 141. On a 153+/flagged binary, verify the UserCancel instanceof branch and the TimeoutError branch render and assert their forwarded telemetry ids.

guidanceConsulted.query: progress bar loading state with retry and cancellation announcements
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Expose progress via role=progressbar with aria-value attributes and announce state changes through polite live text.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The bar is role=progressbar (aria-valuemin/max/now updated per chunk) labelled by the aria-live progress line; outcomes land in a role=status panel.

guidanceConsulted.query: button visual hierarchy primary secondary destructive states
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Secondary actions may invert the fill but must keep an explicit text colour with the background swap.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: button.secondary sets background var(--bg-ivory) AND color var(--text-black) together, avoiding the inherited light-on-light trap.

summary: Practical streaming download with cancel/timeout/complete/retry states. Demonstrates why reason forwarding matters (decoupling the catch site from the controller), shows the honest pre-153 fallback via signal.reason, and was driver-verified through all three outcome branches with a clean console.
